title: Sinusoidal Models
standard_text: P.2O develop and use a sinusoidal function that models a situation in mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on sinusoidal models for Texas TEKS P.2O: amplitude, midline and period from situations, writing and evaluating models, tides and Ferris wheels. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A sinusoidal model is y = A sin(B(t − C)) + D or the same with cos.
  • Amplitude A = (max − min) ÷ 2. Midline D = (max + min) ÷ 2.
  • B = 2π ÷ period.
  • Start at a maximum: use cos. Start on the midline going up: use sin.

Examples

Example

Tide: low 4 ft, high 16 ft, period 12 hours, high at t = 0

A = 6, D = 10

B = 2π ÷ 12 = π/6

Answer: y = 6 cos(π6t) + 10

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The full height as the amplitudeAmplitude is half of max − min.
The period as BB = 2π ÷ period.
Forgetting the midlineAdd D.

faq.a: Develop and use a sinusoidal function that models a situation in mathematical and real-world problems.

faq.q: Can I use sine instead of cosine?
faq.a: Yes, with a phase shift of a quarter period.
Tides, daylight hours, temperatures over a day, and Ferris wheels.

faq.q: Why use radians in the model?
faq.a: The period formula 2π ÷ B uses radians.

sets.title: Amplitude, midline and period from a situation

items.q: The average monthly temperature in a city is modeled by T(m) = 18 sin(πm/6) + 65. What is the period, in months?
items.e: Period = 2π ÷ (π/6) = 12 months, one year.

items.q: At a harbor, high tide is 9 ft and low tide is 1 ft. What are the amplitude and midline of a sine model for the water depth?
items.e: Amplitude = (max − min) ÷ 2 = 4. Midline = (max + min) ÷ 2 = 5. Amplitude 4 ft, midline y = 5 ft.

items.q: The average monthly temperature in a city is modeled by T(m) = 15 sin(πm/6) + 60. What is the period, in months?
items.e: Period = 2π ÷ (π/6) = 12 months, one year.

items.q: A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 100 ft, its center is 60 ft above the ground, and it turns once every 2 minutes. What is the midline of the height function?
items.e: The midline is the height of the center: h = 60 ft.

items.q: A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 120 ft, its center is 63 ft above the ground, and it turns once every 6 minutes. In h(t) = a cos(bt) + d, what is b?
items.e: Period = 2π ÷ b, so b = 2π ÷ 6 = π3.

items.q: A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 50 ft, its center is 35 ft above the ground, and it turns once every 5 minutes. What is the midline of the height function?
items.e: The midline is the height of the center: h = 35 ft.

items.q: A periodic model has period 24. Which value of b should be used in y = sin(bx)?
items.e: b = 2π ÷ period = 2π ÷ 24 = π12.

items.q: A periodic model has period 365. Which value of b should be used in y = sin(bx)?
items.e: b = 2π ÷ period = 2π ÷ 365 = 2π365.

items.q: A Ferris wheel has a diameter of 60 ft, its center is 40 ft above the ground, and it turns once every 10 minutes. What is the amplitude of the height function?

sets.title: When is it at its maximum or minimum?

items.q: h(t) = 3 cos(π5(t − 8)) + 50. At what time t in 0 ≤ t < 10 is h at its maximum?
items.e: Cosine is at its maximum when the inside is 0, at t = 8. t = 8.

items.q: A point moves counterclockwise around a circle of radius 4 centered at the origin, starting at (4, 0). Where is it after turning 11π6?
items.e: The point is (r cos θ, r sin θ) = (4 · √32, 4 · (−12)) = (2√3, −2).

items.q: The point (8, −15) is on the terminal side of an angle θ in standard position. What is sin θ?
items.e: r = √(8² + (−15)²) = 17. Then sin = y/r, cos = x/r, tan = y/x and the reciprocals. sin θ = −1517.

items.q: A Ferris wheel has a radius of 20 ft, and its center is 24 ft above the ground. A seat starts level with the center on the right and turns 240° counterclockwise. To the nearest foot, how high is the seat?
items.e: Height = center + r sin θ = 24 + 20 sin 240° ≈ 24 − 17.3 ≈ 7 ft.

items.q: The point (3, 4) is on the terminal side of an angle θ in standard position. What is sec θ?
items.e: r = √(3² + 4²) = 5. Then sin = y/r, cos = x/r, tan = y/x and the reciprocals. sec θ = 53.

items.q: A Ferris wheel has a radius of 20 ft, and its center is 22 ft above the ground. A seat starts level with the center on the right and turns 210° counterclockwise. To the nearest foot, how high is the seat?
items.e: Height = center + r sin θ = 22 + 20 sin 210° ≈ 22 − 10.0 ≈ 12 ft.
